docs.text: OpenImport ¶ Import and export for Magento 2 and Mage-OS, free and MIT. OpenImport puts profiles, column mapping, value transforms, a dry run that previews every change, schedules and remote sources (SFTP, FTP, URL, server folder) in front of Magento's own import engine. Magento does the writing, so imported data is exactly what core import would produce, and upgrades keep working. Magento's cron must run for schedules and queued runs; bin/magento openimport:doctor tells you whether it does. Where to start ¶ Coming from a paid tool? How OpenImport compares with Firebear, Amasty, Xtento and Magento's own import. Admin : the profile form step by step, the run page, grids and roles. Mapping and filters : columns, store views, auto-match, row filters. Transforms and expressions : what you can do with a value on its way in. Runs, dry runs and safety : what the preview shows, delta mode, the safety threshold, error reports. Sources and Exports : files from somewhere else, files to somewhere else. docs.text: Admin ¶ OpenImport lives under System › Data Transfer : OpenImport Profiles and OpenImport Runs . Settings are under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport . Profiles ¶ The profile list shows each profile's direction, what it imports or exports, its source, schedule and last run. Above it, a status line says how the last 24 hours went (failed runs link to the runs), what is waiting, and whether the cron runs. A click on a row opens the profile. Row actions: Edit , Dry run , Run now (the dialog names the file it imports and how the last dry run went), Duplicate (the copy starts with its schedule off) and Delete (runs and error reports are kept). Mass actions: switch schedules on or off, delete. Import profiles from JSON takes a file from Download as JSON or openimport:profile:export . The form has a step navigation at the top; each step header says what the step holds, and its ? opens the matching page of this documentation. Fields show only where they matter (an export has no import rules, a CSV no sheet name, the cron field only with Custom ), required fields are marked, and a save that fails opens the step with the problem and shows the message at the field. Leaving the form with unsaved changes asks first. Below the steps, Recent runs lists the last five runs of the profile. Download as JSON saves the profile without its secrets. The profile form has six steps: What : name, import or export, and what (Products, Stock & prices, Customers …). Where : the source. For Upload a file , choose the file; it is read on the server, never in the browser. File : format and its options (delimiter, encoding, sheet, record path). The first 20 rows of the file are shown and read again when an option changes. Map : one row per Magento field (pick it from the list, or Other field … to type a code): the column of the file (or a fixed value), the store view, transforms (one without settings is added when chosen; move up and down, remove), empty is an error , and a value map. Auto-match proposes a mapping from the column names (and adds Decimal comma → dot where the file writes numbers with commas), Add required fields adds what Magento needs for new records with proposed fixed values, Preview the first rows shows what Magento will receive, row by row, with any problems. Rules : behaviour (only those the entity can do), rows with errors, allowed errors, skip unchanged rows (delta), safety limit (empty = the configured default), row filters. Order exports have their filters here: statuses, created from/until (date pickers) and which orders. When : manual or a schedule (every 15 or 30 minutes, every hour, every day at a chosen time, presets, or a cron expression) with the next three run times, schedule on/off, e-mails, what happens to the source file after a successful run. Save and dry run saves and starts a dry run straight away. New profiles have their schedule off; switch it on after a dry run you are happy with. Runs ¶ Runs are queued and run by OpenImport's cron within a minute (or by bin/magento openimport:run ). The run page shows the status, the numbers (rows read, new, changed, unchanged, skipped, errors), and refreshes itself while the run is queued or running. Dry runs list what would change: for each record the field, the value now and the value after the run. Run for real imports the very file the dry run checked. Runs with Delete or Replace above the safety limit need the word DELETE or REPLACE typed in, by a role allowed to confirm them ( Confirm runs above the safety limit ). Download error report gives a CSV with the row number, record, field and error, followed by the original row, so you can fix the rows and import them again. Cells that a spreadsheet would run as formulas are protected. Download the file gives the file the run read. Cancel stops a queued run at once, and a running one at its next checkpoint while it still reads the file (before it writes to the shop or sends a file). Run again / Dry run again start the profile again, also from the runs grid. An export's run page shows the first ten rows of the file it wrote. The runs grid can be filtered by what and direction, and searched by profile name. A click on a row opens the run. docs.text: REST API and triggers ¶ Since 1.1. Start a profile from another system ¶ POST /rest/V1/openimport/profiles/{profileId}/runs Authorization: Bearer <integration access token> Content-Type: application/json {"mode": "live"} mode is dry_run (default) or live . The run is queued with the trigger API and OpenImport's cron runs it within a minute, exactly like a scheduled run: same source, mapping, delta, safety threshold (a live run above it waits for a confirmation in the admin) and e-mails. Import profiles need a source other than Upload (folder, URL, SFTP or FTP); exports work with every destination. Answer: {"run_id": 42, "status": "queued", "mode": "live", "message": "", "rows_read": 0, "errors": 0} Ask how it went: GET /rest/V1/openimport/runs/{runId} Access: create an integration (System › Extensions › Integrations) with the resources OpenImport › Run profiles (start) and View runs and error reports (status). Typical use: a PIM or ERP drops a file on the SFTP server and then calls the endpoint, so the import starts at once instead of at the next schedule. Export right after an order is placed ¶ Order export profiles have the setting Also run after every order . When an order is placed (storefront, admin or API), the profile is queued; cron runs it within a minute. Ten orders in that minute make one run, not ten. Combine it with Which orders: Only orders not exported before by this profile so every file holds just the new orders.

docs.text: Archives: ZIP, gzip and tar ¶ Since 1.4. Suppliers often send a products.zip or a stock.csv.gz ; OpenImport unpacks it and reads the file inside, and can pack an export before it is delivered. Reading an archive ¶ Every source (upload, server folder, web address, SFTP, FTP, S3, cloud drives) may deliver an archive. Step 3 of the profile form has two settings: Setting Meaning Archives (ZIP, gzip, tar) Unpack archives (default): a .zip , .gz , .tar , .tar.gz or .tgz file (by name, else by its first bytes) is unpacked and the file inside is read. Read the file as it is : nothing is unpacked. File inside the archive Which file to take out of a ZIP or tar: a name or a pattern ( products-*.csv , data/*.xml , matched against the file name and its path inside the archive, case-insensitive). Empty: the first CSV, TSV, TXT, Excel, ODS, JSON or XML file by name. Hidden files and macOS __MACOSX folders are ignored. A .gz file holds one file, named after the archive ( stock.csv.gz → stock.csv ); a .tar.gz holds a tar. The Format setting and the sample in the form apply to the file inside; the run page names it ("Read products.csv from feed.zip.") and the run's copy is that file, not the archive. After success (move or delete) acts on the archive, as it does on any other source file. Excel ( .xlsx ) and OpenDocument files are ZIP files too; they are never taken for archives. Writing an archive ¶ Compress in step 3 of an export profile packs the written file as .zip , .gz or .tar.gz before it is delivered (download, folder, SFTP, FTP, S3, cloud drive, REST, e-mail). The file name gets the archive's extension ( products-2026-10-21.csv.zip ); the archive holds the file under its own name. Limits and safety ¶ Entry names never become paths: the chosen file is written under a fixed name in the run folder, so an archive with ../../ or absolute names (zip-slip) cannot write anywhere else. Links and devices inside tar files and ZIPs are skipped. The unpacked size is counted while writing, not taken from the archive's headers: more than 1 GB stops the run with a message (zip bombs); the partial file is removed. An archive with more than 10,000 entries is refused. Archives inside archives are not unpacked; password-protected entries are refused; a damaged archive fails the run with a plain message. The limits are arguments of Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Archive\Unpacker in di.xml .

docs.text: Product attributes and attribute sets ¶ Since 1.1. Entity Product attributes and attribute sets ( openimport_attribute ), identifier attribute_code . Import ¶ Add/Update creates attributes that do not exist and updates the given columns of existing ones; it also assigns the attribute to attribute sets. Delete takes the attribute out of the listed attribute sets only: OpenImport never deletes an attribute (its values on every product would go with it). Replace is refused. Column Meaning attribute_code identifier; lower-case letters, digits, underscores label default label; required for a new attribute frontend_input text , textarea , texteditor , select , multiselect , boolean , date , datetime , price , weight ; required for a new attribute, cannot change later options Cotton|Wool|Silk for select and multiselect; options the attribute lacks are added, existing ones keep their ids and order scope global , website or store is_required , is_unique , is_searchable , is_filterable_in_search , is_comparable , is_visible_on_front , used_in_product_listing , is_html_allowed_on_front , is_used_for_promo_rules , used_for_sort_by 1 / 0 (also yes / no , true / false , ja / nein ) is_filterable 0 , 1 (filterable with results) or 2 (filterable, no results) default_value text attribute_set Default, Bags : the sets to assign the attribute to (they must exist) attribute_group the group inside those sets; created when missing; default General Store-view labels work like everywhere in OpenImport: map a file column to store:<store view code>:label for the attribute's label and to store:<store view code>:options for the option labels, in the order of the default options ( Baumwolle|Wolle|Seide ; leave an entry empty to keep the default). The dry run shows the attributes that would be created and every column that would change. Writes go through Magento's attribute repository and attribute management, so the same validation as the admin applies. Export ¶ One row per attribute of the shop's own (user-defined) attributes with options, flags and the sets it belongs to, plus one row per store view with its own label or option labels. Export option attributes = all adds Magento's system attributes. The file imports back as it is.

docs.text: Baseline: core import speed and the core bridge's overhead ¶ Measured in M0 so every later speed claim compares against Magento's own importer, never against another vendor. Method. openimport-dev-env/ci/benchmark.php in the dev-env's Benchmark workflow: Magento Open Source 2.4.9, PHP 8.3, MariaDB 10.6, OpenSearch 2.12, Redis, no sample data, all indexers on "Update by Schedule" , a GitHub Actions runner (4 vCPU, 16 GB). Datasets are generated deterministically by ci/generate-datasets.php : products-10k : 10,000 simple products, 3 categories each (created on the fly), stock, price, a special price on every 7th, an HTML description, plus a German store-view row on every 10th product (11,000 rows); customers-20k : 20,000 customers with one default address ( customer_composite ). Each dataset is imported twice through core's CSV source (create, then the same file again = every entity updated, no value changes) and twice through OpenImport's MappedSource (same rows, other SKUs / e-mails / names). All passes run in one PHP process, so peak memory grows from pass to pass and is shown for orientation only. Results (run 38403542694 , 2026-10-13) ¶ Dataset Path Pass Rows Created Updated Seconds Rows / min products-10k core CSV create 11,000 10,000 10 87.0 7,584 products-10k core CSV update 11,000 0 11,000 89.6 7,363 products-10k OpenImport create 11,000 10,000 10 86.1 7,670 products-10k OpenImport update 11,000 0 11,000 91.8 7,191 customers-20k core CSV create 20,000 20,000 0 24.5 49,077 customers-20k core CSV update 20,000 0 20,000 25.2 47,623 customers-20k OpenImport create 20,000 20,000 0 26.5 45,299 customers-20k OpenImport update 20,000 0 20,000 27.0 44,447 What it says ¶ The core bridge costs almost nothing: products −1 % / +2.5 %, customers +8 % / +7 % (reading the CSV in PHP and building associative rows). The budget in 02 · Architecture is 15 % for the whole pipeline. Re-importing an unchanged catalog costs as much as creating it (90 s for 10k products). A nightly supplier file usually changes a few percent of the rows: delta mode (M1) skips unchanged rows before core sees them. Target: a run with 1 % changed rows takes at most 10 % of a full run. Rate: about 7,500 product rows or 48,000 customer rows per minute on a CI runner with indexers on schedule. Shops with "Update on Save" indexers will be slower; openimport:doctor warns about it. 50,000 products: see below. Configurable products and the full pipeline (readers, mapping, delta) are measured at the end of M1 (memory flat from 10k to 50k is an M1 done-when). 50,000 products (run 38403706606 , 2026-10-13) ¶ Same method, products-50k (50,000 simple products plus 5,000 German store-view rows = 55,000 rows). Path Pass Rows Created Updated Seconds Rows / min core CSV create 55,000 50,000 50 438.6 7,523 core CSV update 55,000 0 55,000 471.6 6,997 OpenImport create 55,000 50,000 50 453.8 7,272 OpenImport update 55,000 0 55,000 497.1 6,639 Core's rate stays flat from 10k to 50k (about 7,500 rows per minute): no slowdown with catalog size at this scale. Bridge overhead +3.5 % (create) and +5.4 % (update), inside the 15 % budget. Peak memory is not comparable between passes here (one process, four passes). The M1 memory check runs each pass in its own process. The whole pipeline (M1, run 38518924669 and 38422135458 , 2026-10-14) ¶ openimport-dev-env/ci/pipeline-benchmark.php : a profile that maps every column 1:1 with transforms on sku, url_key and name, delta on; every pass in its own PHP process ( bin/magento openimport:run ), so peak memory is comparable. Core's own CSV import of the same file runs the same way as the reference. Datasets are generated deterministically by ci/generate-datasets.php : products-10k : 10,000 simple products, 3 categories each (created on the fly), stock, price, a special price on every 7th, an HTML description, plus a German store-view row on every 10th product (11,000 rows); customers-20k : 20,000 customers with one default address ( customer_composite ). Each dataset is imported twice through core's CSV source (create, then the same file again = every entity updated, no value changes) and twice through OpenImport's MappedSource (same rows, other SKUs / e-mails / names). All passes run in one PHP process, so peak memory grows from pass to pass and is shown for orientation only.

docs.text: The core bridge costs almost nothing: products −1 % / +2.5 %, customers +8 % / +7 % (reading the CSV in PHP and building associative rows). The budget in 02 · Architecture is 15 % for the whole pipeline. Re-importing an unchanged catalog costs as much as creating it (90 s for 10k products). A nightly supplier file usually changes a few percent of the rows: delta mode (M1) skips unchanged rows before core sees them. Target: a run with 1 % changed rows takes at most 10 % of a full run. Rate: about 7,500 product rows or 48,000 customer rows per minute on a CI runner with indexers on schedule. Shops with "Update on Save" indexers will be slower; openimport:doctor warns about it. 50,000 products: see below. Configurable products and the full pipeline (readers, mapping, delta) are measured at the end of M1 (memory flat from 10k to 50k is an M1 done-when).

docs.text: Categories ¶ Since 1.1. Import and export categories by path : the names from the root category down, joined with / ( Default Category/Men/Shoes ). A slash inside a name is written \/ . Paths are matched ignoring case; the first segment must be a root category of the shop. Import ¶ Entity Categories ( openimport_category ), behaviours Add/Update and Delete (Replace is refused: Magento would delete and recreate the categories with new ids). Column Meaning path identifier; parents that do not exist yet are created on the way (active, in the menu, named after the segment) name a new category is named after the last segment of its path (a different name is refused, it would make the next import create a duplicate); for an existing category the name column renames it, and its path changes with it url_key , description , meta_title , meta_keywords , meta_description , custom_design , page_layout texts is_active , include_in_menu , is_anchor 1 / 0 , also yes / no , true / false , ja / nein position whole number display_mode PRODUCTS , PAGE or PRODUCTS_AND_PAGE Only the columns a row has are changed, and an empty cell leaves the value as it is ( __EMPTY__VALUE__ clears a default value, as in Magento's import; a name or URL key cannot be cleared). Store-view values are saved one attribute at a time, so a German name does not regenerate the category's URL rewrites (change url_key for that). Store-view values work like everywhere in OpenImport: map a file column to store:<store view code>:<field> ( name_de → Store view de , field name ) and the row sets that store view's value. A shop with only one store view keeps every value in the default scope (that is how Magento saves), so there store-view rows are reported as errors: map the column to the default field instead. The dry run shows the categories that would be created and every field that would change; delete runs count the children too and wait for the typed confirmation above the safety threshold. Writes go through Magento's category model and repository (URL rewrites, indexers and events happen as in the admin), never through raw SQL. Products are assigned to categories through the product import ( categories column), not here. Export ¶ Entity Categories , one row per category with its default values, plus one row per store view that overrides any text ( store_view_code set, only the overridden columns filled). Export option category_rows = default writes default rows only. The file imports back as it is.

docs.text: Command line ¶ bin/magento openimport:profile:list bin/magento openimport:run <profile id or name> [--dry-run] [--file=path] [--full] [--confirm] [--queue] bin/magento openimport:run:status <run id> bin/magento openimport:queue:run [--limit=10] openimport:run ¶ Runs a profile now, in the terminal, and prints the result: status, counts, the first changes (dry runs) and the first errors with the row of the file they come from. Option Effect --dry-run Check and preview only; nothing changes in the shop. --file=path Read this file instead of the profile's source. --full Ignore the delta state: send every row. --confirm Confirm a Delete or Replace run above the safety threshold. --queue Only add the run to the queue; OpenImport's cron runs it. The exit code is 0 for Success and Partial , 1 otherwise, so the command can be used in scripts and deployment pipelines. openimport:run:status ¶ Shows any run (also runs started in the admin or by a schedule) with its counts, changes and errors. openimport:profile:list ¶ Lists all profiles with direction, entity, source, schedule, whether the schedule is active, and the last run. openimport:queue:run ¶ Runs the queued runs now, oldest first (runs started in the admin wait in the queue). OpenImport's cron does the same every minute; the command is for stores without cron, deployments and tests. openimport:secrets:reencrypt ¶ After bin/magento encryption:key:change : encrypts every stored source password, private key and token again with the current key. Run it while the old key is still in app/etc/env.php . openimport:profiles:export [profile …] ¶ Writes profiles as JSON to standard output (all profiles, or the ones named by id or name): every setting, mapping and value map, never passwords, keys, tokens or upload tokens. Keep the file in version control or move it to another store: bin/magento openimport:profiles:export > profiles.json . openimport:profiles:import <file> [--dry-run] ¶ Creates the profiles of such a file; a profile with the same name is updated (its stored secrets are kept). Everything is checked first and listed as "create …" / "update …"; one problem and nothing is saved. --dry-run checks and lists without saving. Enter passwords and keys in the admin afterwards. openimport:doctor ¶ Checks what makes imports slow or stuck and says what to do: cron (has openimport_tick run in the last 10 minutes?), indexers on "Update on Save", PHP extensions and memory_limit , var/openimport writable, runs waiting longer than 15 minutes, runs "running" for more than 90 minutes. Exit code 1 when something needs a look.

Behaviours Add/Update and Delete; Replace is refused (it would change ids that widgets and links use). Column Pages Blocks Meaning identifier ✓ ✓ URL key of a page, identifier of a block stores ✓ ✓ all , or store view codes separated by commas ( default,de ); empty keeps the record's store views (new records: all) title ✓ ✓ required for a new record content ✓ ✓ HTML, Page Builder markup works as it is is_active ✓ ✓ 1 / 0 content_heading , page_layout , meta_title , meta_keywords , meta_description , layout_update_xml , custom_theme , sort_order ✓ page settings An empty cell leaves the value as it is; __EMPTY__VALUE__ clears it (as in Magento's import). Magento allows the same identifier once per store view; OpenImport matches a row to the record with that identifier that is assigned to one of the row's store views (or to all store views). The dry run shows the records that would be created and every column that would change. Writes go through Magento's page and block repositories. Exports write one row per record with the store views as codes; the file imports back as it is (into the same shop or a staging/production twin).

docs.text: Magento writes, not OpenImport. Rows go through Magento_ImportExport , so the result is exactly what core import would produce and upgrades keep working. docs.text: Configurable products from simple rows ¶ Since 1.3. Supplier files usually have one row per variant: a T-shirt in red M, red L and blue M, with a column that names the model they belong to. OpenImport turns such rows into a configurable product with its variants, in the same run. Set it up ¶ Step 4 · Mapping : map the column with the model number to Parent SKU (configurable products) . Map the attributes the variants differ in (color, size …) like any attribute. Optionally map a column to Parent name (configurable products) . Step 5 · Rules : switch on Build configurable products and choose the Variation attributes . Only dropdowns with global scope that the shop defined are offered: Magento accepts only those for variants. Choose what happens to the variants: Not visible on their own (default) or Visibility as mapped . What a run does ¶ Rows with the same parent SKU are the variants of one configurable product. Rows without a parent SKU are imported as they are. After the last row, OpenImport adds the configurable product with all its variants (Magento's configurable_variations ). It takes the values of the first variant in the file (attribute set, websites, categories, description, price, pictures), with: name : Parent name when mapped; otherwise the words all variant names start with ("T-Shirt Basic Red M" and "T-Shirt Basic Blue L" give "T-Shirt Basic"), per store view; visibility Catalog, Search ; URL key from the name; no values for the variation attributes, no quantity, in stock. New variants get the URL key <name>-<sku> when the mapping has no URL key, so variants with equal names do not collide. Existing products keep theirs. The run message says Configurable products: 3 built from 12 variants. The parent's own row ¶ Some files, WooCommerce exports among them, have a row for the parent itself. A row whose product type is configurable and which has no parent SKU is that row: OpenImport sends it once, at the end, with the variations. Its own name, URL key, visibility and stock stay as mapped. Map the file's type column to product_type with a value map ( variable → configurable , variation → simple ). A simple row with a parent's SKU conflicts with that parent: the parent is not built and the run message names it. Rows that cannot be variants ¶ These rows are row errors (the column is named, the rest of the run goes on): Problem Message A variation attribute is empty The variation attribute "size" is empty. A value is not an option of the attribute "Purple" is not an option of color; add it first … Two variants of one parent have the same values Another variant of TS, TS-RED-M, has the same color, size. A row is its own parent The parent SKU is the row's own SKU; a variant needs another parent. A parent SKU is also a variant This SKU is the parent of other rows; it cannot be a variant too. The values must be existing options of the attributes (matched by their admin label, ignoring case, as Magento's import does). Create options with the attribute import first. Skip unchanged rows ¶ With Skip unchanged rows on, unchanged variants are not sent again, but the parent still lists every variant in the file: Magento removes links a parent's list does not name. The parent itself is sent only when its list or values changed. Settings checked before a run ¶ Saving the profile needs the parent SKU column, the variation attributes and their columns. A run stops before reading the file when an attribute is not a global dropdown.

docs.text: Saved connections ¶ Since 1.4. A saved connection is a server login that many profiles share: change the password once, and every profile that uses it logs in with the new one. Open System › Data Transfer › OpenImport Connections . Kind Settings SFTP server, port (empty = 22), user name, password or private key (+ passphrase), time limit FTP server, port (empty = 21), user name, password, explicit TLS (FTPS), passive mode, time limit Amazon S3 / S3-compatible bucket, region, endpoint, path-style addresses, access key, secret key, time limit Google Drive / Sheets a service account key, or a Google account (OAuth client ID and secret, then Sign in with Google ) Dropbox app key and app secret of your Dropbox app, then Sign in with Dropbox OneDrive / SharePoint directory (tenant), client ID and secret of your app registration, SharePoint site (empty = OneDrive), then Sign in with Microsoft REST API base address, login: none, a token in a header, user name and password (Basic) or OAuth 2 client credentials Test connection logs in with what the form holds (saved or not; an empty password field uses the stored one) and reads the login folder: Connected to files.example.com:22. The login folder has 3 file(s). Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage ¶ OpenImport talks to S3 itself (Signature Version 4, no SDK), so the same connection works with Amazon S3 and with services that speak its API: Service Region Endpoint Path-style Amazon S3 the bucket's region, e.g. eu-central-1 empty off Cloudflare R2 auto https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com on or off Wasabi the bucket's region, e.g. eu-central-1 https://s3.eu-central-1.wasabisys.com off MinIO, Garage, SeaweedFS and other self-hosted servers what the server is set up with, often us-east-1 the server's address, e.g. http://minio:9000 on Folders are key prefixes: the profile's folder incoming reads the files incoming/* (not those in deeper folders), Move it to the processed folder copies the file to incoming/processed/ and deletes the original. The access key needs these permissions on the bucket: list ( s3:ListBucket ), read ( s3:GetObject ), and for exports and moving files write and delete ( s3:PutObject , s3:DeleteObject ). Like every address OpenImport reaches, the endpoint must be public. A server in your own network (MinIO on the same host, for example) needs its host name under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety › Private hosts allowed as URL sources . Google Drive and Google Sheets ¶ Two ways to log in: Service account (best for servers): in the Google Cloud console create a project, switch on the Google Drive API , create a service account and a JSON key for it, and paste the key into the connection. The form then shows the account's e-mail address: share the Drive folders (or a Shared Drive) with it, as you would with a person. Google account : create an OAuth client of the type Web application , add the Authorized redirect URI the connection form shows, enter client ID and client secret, save, then click Sign in with Google . OpenImport keeps only the refresh token, encrypted. The connection sees what that person sees. OpenImport runs no service of its own in between: each shop uses its own Google Cloud project. In a profile, the folder is the folder's link ( https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/… ), its id, or a path from My Drive such as Supplier/incoming . Google Sheets in the folder appear as <name>.xlsx and are read as Excel files (every sheet; pick one under the file settings). Move it to the processed folder moves the file into a processed folder next to it (made when missing); Delete it moves it to the Drive bin. Exports upload into the folder; a file with the same name gets the new content and keeps its link. Save as a Google Sheet turns the export into a Google Sheet (named without .csv ), and later exports replace its content. Published "anyone with the link" Sheets still work without a connection as a Web address source. Dropbox ¶ At dropbox.com/developers/apps create an app ( Scoped access ; App folder for a folder of its own, or Full Dropbox ), give it the permissions files.content.read , files.content.write and account_info.read , and add the connection form's Redirect URI under OAuth 2 . Enter app key and app secret in the connection, save, click Sign in with Dropbox . Folders are paths from the top of the Dropbox (or of the app folder): Supplier/incoming . Uploads replace a file of the same name (up to 150 MB per file); Delete it moves the file to Dropbox's deleted files. OneDrive and SharePoint ¶ In Microsoft Entra ID register an app, add the platform Web with the connection form's Redirect URI , create a client secret, and allow the delegated permissions Files.ReadWrite.All , User.Read , offline_access (and Sites.ReadWrite.All for SharePoint sites). Enter directory (tenant) ID or domain (empty = common ), client ID and secret; for a SharePoint document library the site address ( contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/Shop ); save, click Sign in with Microsoft . Folders are paths in the OneDrive or the library: Supplier/incoming . Large files are uploaded in 10 MB parts; Delete it moves the file to the recycle bin. REST APIs ¶ A REST connection holds the API's base address ( https://api.example.com/v1 ) and its login; profiles add their own path ( /products?status=active ). The login is a header with a token ( Authorization: Bearer … , X-Api-Key: … ), Basic user name and password, or OAuth 2 client credentials (token address, client ID and secret, optional scope; the token is fetched and renewed by OpenImport). When an API answers 429 Too Many Requests or 503 , OpenImport waits as its Retry-After says (up to 30 seconds) and tries again, three times at most. As a source , the profile names where the records are in the JSON answer (a dotted path such as data.items ; empty = the answer itself, or its first list) and how the API pages: Pages Settings One answer – Page numbers page parameter ( page ), first page (1), optional page size parameter and size ( per_page , 100) Offsets offset parameter ( offset ), first offset (0), optional size parameter and size ( limit , 100) A cursor in the answer where the cursor is ( meta.next_cursor ) and its parameter ( cursor ) The next address in the answer where it is ( links.next ); it must be on the API's host The Link header – ( rel="next" ) Pages stop at an empty page, a shorter page (with a size parameter) or when there is no next cursor or address. Pages at most (100) protects against endless paging: a run that reaches it stops with an error and imports nothing, so a partial list never counts as the complete list. Nested fields become columns such as stock.qty ; map them as usual. As an export destination , the file is sent as it is (POST or PUT, with the content type of the format), or, for JSON exports, the records go in batches of a chosen size, each a JSON list. Using a connection in a profile ¶ In step 2 of a profile, choose SFTP, FTP, Amazon S3, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive / SharePoint or a REST API as the source (or as the export destination), then pick the connection under Saved connection . The login fields disappear; the profile keeps only what is its own: the folder, the file pattern, which file to read and what to do with it after a successful run. For SFTP and FTP, Enter the login here keeps the login in the profile, as before 1.4; S3 and the cloud drives always use a saved connection. Only connections of the chosen kind are offered. A profile whose connection was deleted or changed to another kind cannot be saved and its runs fail with a plain message ( The saved connection "Supplier" is for SFTP, not for FTP. ). Deleting ¶ A connection that a profile uses cannot be deleted; the message names the profiles. The grid shows which profiles use each connection. Secrets ¶ Passwords, private keys and passphrases are encrypted with Magento's key, never sent back to the form and never logged. After bin/magento encryption:key:change , bin/magento openimport:secrets:reencrypt encrypts the secrets of profiles and connections again. Profiles as JSON ¶ A profile file names its connection ( "connection": "Supplier SFTP" in source_config or export_options ), never its id or login. Importing the file on another shop needs a connection with that name there; otherwise the import stops before anything is saved and says which connection is missing. Permissions ¶ The admin role resource OpenImport › Manage connections opens the connections grid and form. Choosing a saved connection in a profile only needs the profile permissions.

docs.text: Core bridge: how OpenImport writes data ¶ OpenImport never writes catalog, customer or stock tables itself. It prepares rows (read the file, map columns, transform values, filter rows) and hands them to Magento's own import engine, the one behind System › Data Transfer › Import. Whatever core would write for an equivalent CSV file is what OpenImport writes. The pieces ¶ Class Job Model\Source\MappedSource Core's AbstractSource over OpenImport's prepared rows. No temporary CSV file: core pulls rows from a generator. Missing columns become empty cells, like an empty CSV cell ("leave unchanged"). Model\Bridge\CoreImport Core's Import model plus getBunchIds() : the importexport_importdata rows this import validated (2.4.9 has getValidatedIds() , 2.4.7 and 2.4.8 do not). Model\Bridge\CoreImporter Validate, then (live runs only) add a core import history row, import, invalidate the entity's indexers, and always remove this run's bunches. Model\Bridge\ImportRequest / ImportResult / RowError What to run, and what came back (counts, errors with 0-based row positions, history id, time). Why the bunches are removed ¶ Core validation stores the validated rows in importexport_importdata and later imports the bunches whose ids the entity adapter collected. A dry run validates and stops, so its bunches would stay in the table. They are deleted by id at the end of every run, dry or live, and also when core throws. Import history ¶ Core's import updates the most recent history row of the current admin user (2.4.7, 2.4.8) or the row named in _import_history_id (2.4.9). A live OpenImport run adds its own history row right before the import and passes its id, so core's updates land on OpenImport's row on every version, never on someone else's import. The run appears under System › Data Transfer › Import History with its summary. The history row has no downloadable file yet (M1 writes the mapped rows there). Evidence ¶ Test/Integration/Bridge/CoreBridgeTest.php imports the same rows twice, once through core's CSV source (the admin path) and once through MappedSource , and compares the results field by field: simple products: new products with stock, special price, HTML description, disabled status, "Not Visible Individually", a store-view row; updates including __EMPTY__VALUE__ ; Replace and Delete; customers; dry run: nothing written, no bunch left behind; invalid rows with "skip errors": reported with their 0-based position, same outcome as core's CSV import; nothing imported with "stop on error"; import history row written and completed. Magento PHP Result (CI run 38402758703 ) 2.4.7-p10 8.2, 8.3 11 / 11 green 2.4.8-p5 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 11 / 11 green 2.4.9 8.3, 8.4 11 / 11 green Decision: MappedSource straight into core on every supported version. The temporary-CSV fallback planned in 02 · Architecture is not needed and is not built. What the spike found ¶ Core's error aggregator is shared. ProcessingErrorAggregator is a DI singleton. Core runs one import per admin request; OpenImport runs many per process (cron, CLI). Without clear() before each run, errors of earlier runs counted against the next run and stopped valid imports. docs.text: Exports ¶ An export profile (direction Export ) writes a file from a Magento export entity: products, customers, customer addresses, advanced pricing, stock sources (MSI) — every entity Magento's own System › Data Transfer › Export offers — plus OpenImport's Orders export. The rows come from Magento's own export code, so the columns are exactly those of a core export; OpenImport adds row filters, column mapping, formats and destinations, and runs it on a schedule. Steps ¶ What : direction Export and the entity. Where : the destination (download from the run page, server folder, SFTP, FTP, Amazon S3 or S3-compatible, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive / SharePoint, a REST API, e-mail) and the file name. Placeholders in the file name: {entity} , {profile} , {date} (2026-10-14), {time} (143000), {datetime} , {run} , {ext} . Default {entity}-{datetime}.{ext} . File : CSV (delimiter, encoding UTF-8, Windows-1252 or ISO-8859-1/-15, BOM, line ending, header row on or off), Excel (.xlsx, sheet name), JSON (root key, pretty) or XML (root and record element names). Map : without a mapping every column is written as Magento exports it. With a mapping, each row is one column of the file: its name, the Magento column it comes from (or a fixed value), transforms and value maps — for example Preis = price with number(2, ",") for a German decimal comma. Rules : row filters on the Magento columns ( price > 15 , status in pending,processing , …). core_filters (attribute => value) are passed to Magento's export filter as well, for example sku = SUP- for a "like" filter. When : schedule, e-mails, and for orders "only new since the last run". A dry run writes the file into the run folder (download it from the run page to check it) but delivers it nowhere. A live run delivers it and keeps a copy in the run folder for "Keep run files for" days. Safety ¶ Cells that would run as a formula in a spreadsheet ( = , + , - , @ , tab, CR first) are prefixed with ' in CSV and Excel files (Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety › Protect exports against spreadsheet formulas ). Negative numbers are left alone. Excel files are written without any library: plain numbers become numeric cells, everything else stays text (SKUs with leading zeros survive). Excel's limit of 1,048,575 rows is enforced with a plain message. Destinations use the same encrypted secrets and the same SSRF, path and folder rules as sources (see Sources ). Orders ¶ The Orders entity is OpenImport's own (Magento has no order export). One row per order line by default (order, customer, totals, billing and shipping address, payment, shipments and tracking numbers repeated on every line; child lines of configurable and bundle products left out unless chosen), or one row per order. Filters: statuses, created from/until (in the store time zone of Stores › Configuration › General › Locale, like the schedules; a date alone as "until" counts the whole day), store views, and Which orders : all, only orders this profile has not exported before, or new and changed orders (an order whose updated_at moved after its export, for status changes). Exported orders are remembered per profile ( openimport_export_mark ) after a successful live run; dry runs remember nothing. Typical use: a nightly "new orders" file for an ERP over SFTP. Columns: increment_id , state , status , created_at , updated_at , store_code , store_name , customer_email , customer_firstname , customer_lastname , customer_group , customer_is_guest , order_currency_code , subtotal , subtotal_incl_tax , discount_amount , discount_description , coupon_code , shipping_amount , shipping_incl_tax , tax_amount , grand_total , total_paid , total_refunded , total_due , total_qty_ordered , weight , shipping_method , shipping_description , payment_method , payment_last_trans_id , payment_po_number , customer_note , shipment_increment_ids , tracking_numbers , tracking_carriers , remote_ip , billing_* and shipping_* (firstname, lastname, company, street, city, postcode, region, country_id, telephone, email, vat_id), and per line item_id , item_sku , item_name , item_product_type , item_parent_sku , item_qty_ordered , item_qty_invoiced , item_qty_shipped , item_qty_refunded , item_qty_canceled , item_price , item_price_incl_tax , item_row_total , item_row_total_incl_tax , item_discount_amount , item_tax_amount , item_tax_percent , item_weight , item_product_options . Amounts are in the order's currency without trailing zeros. The same layout is what the order import reads. Destinations ¶ XSLT after writing (XML) reshapes an XML export into any layout before it is delivered, see XSLT ; Compress (step 3) packs the file as .zip , .gz or .tar.gz before it goes to any destination; see Archives . Download : the file stays in the run folder, with a button on the run page. Server folder : under var/openimport/<path> or an allowed absolute folder (created when missing). A file of the same name is kept and the new one gets the date and time, or overwritten (profile setting). SFTP / FTP : uploaded into the remote folder; same login settings and secrets as sources, or a saved connection . Google Drive / Sheets : uploaded into the Drive folder of a saved Google connection ; optionally as a Google Sheet. Dropbox , OneDrive / SharePoint : uploaded into the folder of a saved connection ; a file of the same name is replaced. REST API : the file (POST or PUT) or, for JSON exports, the records in batches; see REST APIs . Amazon S3 / S3-compatible : uploaded into the folder (key prefix) of the bucket of a saved S3 connection . E-mail : attached (up to 10 MB) to an e-mail sent through the store's mail settings, template OpenImport: an exported file .

docs.text: File formats ¶ OpenImport reads CSV, Excel (.xlsx), JSON and XML files without any extra library. The format comes from the profile, or is detected from the file name and, when the name says nothing, from the first bytes of the file. Every reader returns rows of text keyed by column name, and every row keeps its position in the file, so an error says "row 18" and row 18 is what the merchant sees in Excel or a text editor. CSV and TSV ¶ Option Default Notes Delimiter auto Detected from the header line: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe (counted outside quotes). Enclosure " Doubled enclosures inside a cell ( "" ) are one quote. Encoding auto UTF-8 (with or without byte order mark), UTF-16 with byte order mark (Excel "Unicode text"), otherwise Windows-1252. Can be set to UTF-8, Windows-1252, ISO-8859-1 or ISO-8859-15. First row is the header yes Without a header, columns are named column_1 , column_2 , … Quoted cells may hold delimiters and line breaks. Empty lines are skipped; row numbers still count them. Empty header cells become column_<n> ; duplicate headers become name (2) , name (3) . Short rows are filled with empty cells; extra cells without a header are dropped. The file is streamed: memory does not grow with the file size. Excel (.xlsx) ¶ Option Default Notes Sheet first sheet A sheet name (case does not matter) or its position (1, 2, …). First row is the header yes Text, numbers, booleans ( 1 / 0 ) and the cached results of formulas are read. Error cells ( #N/A ) are empty. Numbers come out as Excel shows them, without binary noise ( 0.3 , not 0.30000000000000004 ). Cells with a date or time format become 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31 14:30:00 (1900 and 1904 date systems). Row numbers are the sheet's own row numbers; empty rows are skipped. Old Excel files (.xls) are not supported: save them as .xlsx or .csv. Workbooks that would unpack to more than 512 MB are refused. The sheet is streamed with PHP's XMLReader; only the shared strings table is held in memory. OpenDocument (.ods) ¶ Since 1.4. LibreOffice Calc, Collabora and OnlyOffice spreadsheets, with the same options as Excel (sheet by name or position, header row). Typed cells are read by their value: numbers without display formatting ( 12.5 , not 12,50 € ), dates and times as 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31 14:30:00 , booleans as 1 / 0 ; everything else as the cell's text (several paragraphs joined by a line break). Comments (annotations) are left out. Repeated cells and rows, as Calc writes them for the unused area, are expanded; empty rows and trailing empty cells are dropped. Row numbers are the sheet's own. Exports write one sheet with a bold header row; numbers as numbers, text as text (formula guard as for CSV). Streamed with XMLReader; files with a DOCTYPE, files that are no spreadsheet (an .odt text) and files that would unpack to more than 512 MB are refused. JSON ¶ Option Default Notes Record path auto A dot path to the list of records, e.g. data.items . Auto: the document itself when it is a list, otherwise its only list of objects. Nested objects become dotted columns: {"stock": {"qty": 3}} gives the column stock.qty . Lists of plain values are joined with a comma ( ["red", "blue"] gives red,blue ); lists of objects are kept as JSON text in one column, for a transform to pick apart. true / false become 1 / 0 , null becomes an empty cell. Very large integers keep every digit. JSON files are read into memory, up to 50 MB by default. Use CSV or XML for larger files. XML ¶ Option Default Notes Record path children of the root /catalog/products/product (from the root) or //product (at any depth). Child elements become columns ( sku , stock.qty ), attributes become @id or price.@currency . Repeated plain children are joined with a comma ( <category>Men</category><category>Sale</category> gives Men,Sale ); repeated children with their own children are kept as JSON text. CDATA is read as text. The file is streamed record by record: memory does not grow with the file size. Files with a DOCTYPE are refused, and the parser never loads anything from the network (no XML entity attacks). XSLT (since 1.4) ¶ A supplier's XML rarely has one element per record. XSLT before reading (XML) in step 3 takes an XSLT 1.0 stylesheet that turns the file into the XML OpenImport reads, before the reader and the sample see it; XSLT after writing (XML) in an export profile reshapes the written file (root and record names as set) into any layout a partner wants, before it is delivered. Example for an import: <xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"> <xsl:template match="/"> <products> <xsl:for-each select="lieferung/artikel"> <product> <sku><xsl:value-of select="@nr"/></sku> <name><xsl:value-of select="bezeichnung"/></name> <price><xsl:value-of select="translate(vk, ',', '.')"/></price> </product> </xsl:for-each> </products> </xsl:template> </xsl:stylesheet> Safety: the stylesheet and the file are parsed without network access and without DOCTYPE; the processor may read nothing from disk or the network ( document() , xsl:include and xsl:import are refused) and write nothing; PHP functions are not available. The whole file is held in memory for the transformation, so files above 64 MB are refused ( Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Xslt\XsltStep in di.xml ); the stylesheet is checked when the profile is saved. Needs PHP's ext-xsl , which Magento requires anyway. Column names in JSON and XML files ¶ JSON and XML records do not all need the same fields. The column list shown in the mapping editor comes from the first 1,000 records; fields that only appear later are still imported when they are mapped by name.

Typed cells are read by their value: numbers without display formatting ( 12.5 , not 12,50 € ), dates and times as 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31 14:30:00 , booleans as 1 / 0 ; everything else as the cell's text (several paragraphs joined by a line break). Comments (annotations) are left out. Repeated cells and rows, as Calc writes them for the unused area, are expanded; empty rows and trailing empty cells are dropped. Row numbers are the sheet's own. Exports write one sheet with a bold header row; numbers as numbers, text as text (formula guard as for CSV). Streamed with XMLReader; files with a DOCTYPE, files that are no spreadsheet (an .odt text) and files that would unpack to more than 512 MB are refused.

docs.text: Option Default Notes Record path auto A dot path to the list of records, e.g. data.items . Auto: the document itself when it is a list, otherwise its only list of objects. Nested objects become dotted columns: {"stock": {"qty": 3}} gives the column stock.qty . Lists of plain values are joined with a comma ( ["red", "blue"] gives red,blue ); lists of objects are kept as JSON text in one column, for a transform to pick apart. true / false become 1 / 0 , null becomes an empty cell. Very large integers keep every digit. JSON files are read into memory, up to 50 MB by default. Use CSV or XML for larger files.
docs.title: JSON

docs.text: Option Default Notes Record path children of the root /catalog/products/product (from the root) or //product (at any depth). Child elements become columns ( sku , stock.qty ), attributes become @id or price.@currency . Repeated plain children are joined with a comma ( <category>Men</category><category>Sale</category> gives Men,Sale ); repeated children with their own children are kept as JSON text. CDATA is read as text. The file is streamed record by record: memory does not grow with the file size. Files with a DOCTYPE are refused, and the parser never loads anything from the network (no XML entity attacks).
docs.title: XML

docs.text: A supplier's XML rarely has one element per record. XSLT before reading (XML) in step 3 takes an XSLT 1.0 stylesheet that turns the file into the XML OpenImport reads, before the reader and the sample see it; XSLT after writing (XML) in an export profile reshapes the written file (root and record names as set) into any layout a partner wants, before it is delivered. Example for an import: <xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"> <xsl:template match="/"> <products> <xsl:for-each select="lieferung/artikel"> <product> <sku><xsl:value-of select="@nr"/></sku> <name><xsl:value-of select="bezeichnung"/></name> <price><xsl:value-of select="translate(vk, ',', '.')"/></price> </product> </xsl:for-each> </products> </xsl:template> </xsl:stylesheet> Safety: the stylesheet and the file are parsed without network access and without DOCTYPE; the processor may read nothing from disk or the network ( document() , xsl:include and xsl:import are refused) and write nothing; PHP functions are not available. The whole file is held in memory for the transformation, so files above 64 MB are refused ( Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Xslt\XsltStep in di.xml ); the stylesheet is checked when the profile is saved. Needs PHP's ext-xsl , which Magento requires anyway.

docs.text: Product pictures ¶ Product imports take pictures in the same columns as Magento's own import: base_image , small_image , thumbnail_image , swatch_image , additional_images (several, separated by commas), hide_from_product_page and any custom image attribute. A cell can hold a web address or a file name . Pictures from web addresses ¶ OpenImport downloads every http:// or https:// picture itself before Magento sees the row, and hands Magento the downloaded file. Magento never downloads a picture on its own, so: Safe. Every address, and every redirect on the way, goes through the same check as URL sources: private, local and link-local addresses are refused unless an administrator allows the host under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety . Only http and https are read. Checked. A picture must be a JPG, PNG or GIF, told by its first bytes, not by its address or by what the server claims. A web page sent instead of a picture (an error page with status 200, a login page) is refused with a clear message. WebP, AVIF and SVG are refused because Magento's product import does not accept them. Capped. Pictures larger than Largest picture (MB) (10 by default) or slower than Time per picture (30 seconds) count as unreachable. Downloaded once. Each address is downloaded once per run, however many rows and columns use it. Downloaded pictures are kept in var/import/images/openimport . For Check for changed pictures after (hours) (24 by default) the kept file is used without asking the server. After that the next run asks with the server's ETag and Last-Modified (a conditional request) and downloads only pictures that changed. Set it to 0 to ask on every run. Robust. When a server cannot be reached but the picture was downloaded before, the earlier file is used. Good names. The kept file has the name from the address ( …/Red%20Shoe.JPG becomes red-shoe.jpg ). Magento names the catalog file after it. The folder comes from the content's checksum, so a changed picture gets a new file and equal pictures share one. Dry runs download too, so a dry run tells you which pictures cannot be read and the live run finds them ready. The run message counts the pictures: Pictures: 12 downloaded, 230 unchanged, 1 could not be read. When a picture cannot be read ¶ Step 5 of the profile, Pictures that cannot be read : Choice What happens Report the row as an error (default) The row is a row error, with the address and the reason ( HTTP 404 , a web page, not a picture , …). Rows with errors and Errors allowed decide the rest, as for any row error. Import the row without the picture The row is imported; the picture's cell is left empty, which keeps the product's current picture. The run message names the first five rows and pictures left out. With Skip unchanged rows on, a row imported without a picture is not remembered as done: the next run tries the picture again. Pictures from file names ¶ A cell without :// is a file name. Magento reads it from the import images folder, var/import/images (the Images Upload Directory under Stores › Configuration › Advanced › System ), the same folder Magento's own import uses. Sub folders work: supplier/red-shoe.jpg is var/import/images/supplier/red-shoe.jpg . Changed in 1.3. Before 1.3 OpenImport left the folder to Magento's default for imports started by code, pub/media/import . Move pictures you placed there to var/import/images . Housekeeping ¶ Downloaded pictures no run used for Keep unused downloaded pictures for (days) (30 by default) are removed from var/import/images/openimport by the OpenImport housekeeping cron. Pictures already copied into the catalog stay. Settings ¶ Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Pictures from web addresses : Setting Default Check for changed pictures after (hours) 24 Largest picture (MB) 10 Time per picture (seconds) 30 Keep unused downloaded pictures for (days) 30

docs.text: Mapping, store views and row filters ¶ Mapping ¶ A profile maps Magento fields (core import columns) to the file: Source column : the value comes from that column of the file. Fixed value : the same value for every row (for example attribute_set_code = Default , _website = base ). Transforms : an ordered list applied to the value (see Transforms and expressions ). A field with no source column and an expr transform computes its value from the whole row. Required : an empty result makes the row an error instead of sending it. Magento fields that are not mapped are not sent, so Magento leaves them unchanged. Columns of the file that are not mapped are ignored. The identifier field of the entity must be mapped: Entity Identifier Products ( catalog_product ), Stock & prices sku Advanced pricing sku , tier_price_website , tier_price_customer_group , tier_price_qty Customers, customers with address email , _website Customer addresses _email , _website , _entity_id Stock sources (MSI) sku , source_code Stock & prices ¶ The Stock & prices entity ( openimport_stock_price ) is made for supplier feeds: it can set qty , is_in_stock , price , special_price , special_price_from_date , special_price_to_date and cost of products that already exist, through Magento's own product import (with MSI, qty goes to the default source). SKUs the shop does not have are skipped and counted as skipped by behaviour ; they are never created. For quantities per MSI source, use the Stock sources entity. Auto-match ¶ The mapping editor suggests a mapping from the file's column names, in this order: the exact name; the name ignoring case, spaces, underscores, hyphens and dots ( Special Price → special_price ); known synonyms ( Artikelnummer → sku , Bestand / Menge → qty , Preis → price , Bezeichnung → name , E-Mail → email , Vorname → firstname …); and store-view columns ( name_de , name (de) , name [de] , store:de:name ). Each column is used once. When the first rows of a number field (price, cost, weight, qty …) are written with decimal commas ( 89,90 , 1.299,00 ), Auto-match adds the transform Decimal comma → dot to that field. Add required fields adds the fields Magento needs for new records with a proposed fixed value where there is a sensible one: the shop's default attribute set and website, product type simple , the default customer group, the default inventory source. Pick a column of the file instead, or change the value. Store-view values (products) ¶ Map a field as store:<store view code>:<field> , for example store:de:name . One row of the file then becomes the default row plus one row per store view that has at least one non-empty value. Store-view rows carry the SKU, the attribute set and the product type (Magento needs those for new products) and the store-view fields only. Row filters ¶ Row filters decide which rows of the file are imported, before mapping: Mode : include imports only the matching rows; exclude skips them. Match : all conditions or any condition. Conditions : a column, an operator and a value, or an expression . Operator Matches when the cell (trimmed, ignoring case) … equals , not_equals is / is not the value contains , not_contains , starts_with , ends_with contains / starts / ends with the value in , not_in is / is not one of a comma-separated list empty , not_empty is empty / not empty (a missing column is empty) greater_than , less_than is a number above / below the value (decimal commas allowed) regex matches the pattern Rows skipped by a filter are counted as "skipped by filter" on the run page, not as errors.

docs.text: Products missing from the file ¶ Since 1.3. When a supplier sends the complete list of what it sells, products it no longer lists should not stay for sale. Step 5 of a product profile, Products missing from the file : Choice What happens to a product in the scope that the file does not name Leave them (default) nothing Disable them status Disabled (only enabled products are counted) Set them out of stock quantity 0, Out of stock (only products in stock are counted) Delete them deleted Scope decides which products the list covers: All products ; Products of a website (choose the website); Products with an attribute value , for example supplier = Acme : the right choice when several suppliers fill one catalog. For dropdowns enter the option label. How it works ¶ The run reads the whole file. Every SKU in it counts as named: also rows the row filters leave out, rows with errors, rows Skip unchanged rows leaves out and configurable parents OpenImport builds. After the last row OpenImport asks the shop for the products in the scope and keeps those the file does not name. Magento imports the file, then the change for the missing products goes through Magento's import too (status, stock or delete), as one more step of the same run. The run message names them: Products missing from the file: disabled 2 (A-4, A-5). The dry run says what it would do ( would disable 2 … ) and changes nothing. Safety ¶ Rows with errors stop it. When OpenImport could not prepare a row, that row may name a product, so nothing is disabled, set out of stock or deleted. The run message says so. Safety limit. When the missing products are more than the profile's safety limit (share of the products in the scope), the run waits for a typed confirmation: Type DISABLE to confirm (or OUT OF STOCK , DELETE ). The dry run shows the same note. On the command line use --confirm . It works with the behaviours Add/Update and Only update existing . Stock: Set them out of stock writes Magento's default stock (with MSI: the default source), like the qty and is_in_stock columns of Magento's product import.

docs.text: Order import ¶ Since 1.5. Entity Orders ( openimport_order ), direction import. Historic orders — from an old shop, another Magento, an ERP, or OpenImport's own order export — land in sales_order as they are : the file's state and status, created date, totals, addresses, items and the recorded payment method. Nothing is quoted, priced, charged or e-mailed; the shop's current prices, taxes, shipping rates and payment settings play no part. Optionally the invoices, shipments (with tracking numbers) and credit memos are created from the quantities in the file, and the stock is reduced. Orders are only added (behaviour Add/Update or Only add ): an order number that exists is skipped and reported, the run ends as partial . Nothing updates, replaces or deletes an order. The file ¶ One row per order line, the layout of the order export : the first row of an order carries the order, every row one item. Rows of one order are grouped by increment_id and may sit anywhere in the file. Export an order from a store with the Orders export (per line) to see every column with real values. Required for every order: increment_id , customer_email , status (or state ), billing_firstname , billing_lastname , billing_street , billing_city , billing_country_id , and per row item_sku , item_qty_ordered , item_price . The rest is optional. Columns Meaning increment_id The order number. With Keep the file's numbers it becomes the shop's order number; with Generate new numbers it only groups the rows and the store's next number is used (the file's number is noted in the order comment). state , status Any status of Stores › Order Status; the state comes from the status when empty. A state alone takes the state's default status. created_at The order date ( 2024-03-01 14:02:00 , in UTC like the export); empty: now. store_code The store view ( default ); empty: the default store view. customer_email , customer_firstname , customer_lastname , customer_group , customer_is_guest A customer with that e-mail on the store's website is linked to the order; otherwise the order is a guest order with the names of the file. The group by code ( General ) or id; empty: the customer's group or NOT LOGGED IN . order_currency_code ISO code; empty: the store's base currency. Base amounts are copied from the order amounts (rate 1). subtotal , discount_amount , shipping_amount , tax_amount , grand_total , total_paid , total_refunded , total_due , total_qty_ordered , weight , subtotal_incl_tax , shipping_incl_tax Taken from the file. Empty subtotal , total_qty_ordered and grand_total are computed from the items; given ones must match (subtotal = Σ row totals; grand total = subtotal + shipping + tax − discount, 1 cent tolerance). total_due empty: grand total − paid. discount_description , coupon_code Recorded on the order; no rule is applied or counted. shipping_method , shipping_description flatrate_flatrate and its title, as recorded. Nothing is rated. payment_method , payment_last_trans_id , payment_po_number The method code ( checkmo , banktransfer , paypal_express …), recorded as the order's payment; empty: checkmo . Nothing is charged. customer_note , remote_ip Recorded. tracking_numbers , tracking_carriers ; -separated, used by Create invoices, shipments and credit memos : one shipment with these tracking numbers (carrier codes, or custom ). billing_* , shipping_* firstname , lastname , company , street (lines separated by , or a line break), city , postcode , region , country_id , telephone , email , vat_id . No shipping address: the billing address is used. item_sku , item_name , item_product_type , item_parent_sku , item_qty_ordered , item_qty_invoiced , item_qty_shipped , item_qty_refunded , item_qty_canceled , item_price , item_price_incl_tax , item_row_total , item_row_total_incl_tax , item_discount_amount , item_tax_amount , item_tax_percent , item_weight , item_product_options One item per row. A SKU that exists in the catalogue links the product (id, type); a SKU that doesn't is kept as an item of a deleted product, as Magento keeps them. item_parent_sku names the parent of a configurable or bundle child in the same order (children carry no row total). item_product_options is the JSON of the export (chosen options, for the admin's order view). Empty item_row_total : price × quantity. Options ¶ Under Import options when the entity is Orders : Order numbers : Keep the file's numbers (the default; an order with that number is skipped) or Generate new numbers from the store's sequence, for a file whose numbers clash with the shop's own. Create invoices, shipments and credit memos : from item_qty_invoiced , item_qty_shipped (with the tracking numbers) and item_qty_refunded , through Magento's own services — offline, nothing is charged or refunded, no e-mails. Afterwards the file's state, status and paid/refunded/due totals are set again, so a complete order stays complete. Off: the order carries the quantities as numbers but has no documents. Reduce stock : subtract the ordered quantities from the products' stock (simple, virtual and downloadable items), as a new order would. Off (the default): historic orders leave the stock alone. What a run does ¶ Every order is checked first: e-mail, status, group, date, currency, numbers, the billing address, items with a quantity and a price, parents present, totals consistent. A dry run counts the orders that would be created and names every problem with the file's row number; nothing is written. One transaction per order: an order whose creation fails (a database error, a document service refusing) is rolled back and reported; the others are kept. Every imported order gets a history comment Imported by OpenImport (order … in the file) . Orders that exist already are skipped and reported, so a file can be imported twice without duplicates. Auto-match knows the export's column names and Bestellnummer , order number , E-Mail , SKU , Menge and the like. Round trip ¶ The order import is tested against the order export: the test exports Magento's fixture orders per line, imports the file with new numbers, exports the new orders and compares the rows. What the export writes, the import reads. A migration from another OpenImport store is therefore: export orders per line → import with Keep the file's numbers and Create invoices, shipments and credit memos . Sample file (two orders, three lines): increment_id;status;created_at;customer_email;customer_firstname;customer_lastname;order_currency_code;subtotal;shipping_amount;grand_total;total_paid;shipping_method;payment_method;billing_firstname;billing_lastname;billing_street;billing_city;billing_postcode;billing_country_id;item_sku;item_name;item_qty_ordered;item_qty_invoiced;item_qty_shipped;item_price 2019-4711;complete;2019-05-02 09:12:00;anna@example.com;Anna;Berg;EUR;39.9;4.9;44.8;44.8;flatrate_flatrate;banktransfer;Anna;Berg;Ringstraße 7;Wien;1010;AT;SHIRT-RED-M;Red shirt M;1;1;1;19.95 2019-4711;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;;SHIRT-RED-L;Red shirt L;1;1;1;19.95 2019-4712;canceled;2019-05-03 18:40:00;ben@example.com;Ben;Kurz;EUR;59;0;59;0;flatrate_flatrate;checkmo;Ben;Kurz;Am Markt 2;Graz;8010;AT;JACKET-BLK;Black jacket;1;0;0;59

docs.text: Cart and catalog price rules ¶ Since 1.5. Two entities, import and export: Cart price rules and coupons ( openimport_cart_rule , Marketing › Cart Price Rules ) and Catalog price rules ( openimport_catalog_rule , Marketing › Catalog Price Rules ). A file of rules — seasonal discounts, a coupon campaign, the price rules of another store — lands in Magento's rules through the rule models the admin forms use. The export writes every rule with its conditions as JSON, and the file imports back as it is, into the same or another store. Rules are matched by name ( rule_id when the file has one, which the export writes). Add/Update creates or updates — empty columns of an existing rule keep their values — Delete removes the rules named in the file, Replace is refused. Two rules with the same name in the shop are reported; add the rule_id column to say which one. Columns of both ¶ Column Required Meaning name yes The rule's name. rule_id no Magento's id, to update a rule whose name changes. description , is_active , priority , stop_rules_processing no As in the admin form ( priority = Priority / sort order). New rules: active, priority 0. websites no Website codes, comma-separated, or all . New rules: all websites. customer_groups no Customer group codes ( NOT LOGGED IN , General , …), comma-separated, or all . New rules: all groups. from_date , to_date no 2026-11-01 ; empty: no limit. action new rules Cart: by_percent , by_fixed , cart_fixed , buy_x_get_y . Catalog: by_percent , by_fixed , to_percent , to_fixed . discount_amount new rules The percentage or amount. condition_skus no SKUs, comma-separated: the rule applies when such a product is in the cart (cart) or to these products (catalog). condition_categories no Category paths ( Default Category/Sale ), comma-separated, likewise. conditions no Magento's condition tree as JSON, for everything the simple columns cannot say (see below). When filled, the simple condition columns are ignored. Columns of cart price rules ¶ Column Meaning coupon_type none (the default), specific (a code) or auto (Magento generates codes). Empty with a coupon_code : specific. coupon_code The coupon code of the rule. coupon_codes Several codes of one rule, separated by ; or , — a code list from a campaign. The rule then works like Magento's Use Auto Generation (a coupon_code given as well joins the list). Codes the rule has already are kept; a code of another rule is an error. uses_per_coupon , uses_per_customer Limits; 0 = unlimited. discount_qty , discount_step Maximum Qty Discount is Applied To , Discount Qty Step (Buy X) . apply_to_shipping 1 / 0 . free_shipping no , matching (for matching items only) or cart (for the whole order with matching items). labels What the customer sees: a default label, and per store view code:label , separated by \| : 10 % off\|de:10 % Rabatt . condition_subtotal The rule applies from this subtotal on ( base_subtotal >= X ). action_skus , action_categories Which items get the discount ( Apply the rule only to cart items matching… ); empty: all items of the cart. actions The action condition tree as JSON (when filled, action_skus and action_categories are ignored). Conditions as JSON ¶ The conditions (and actions ) columns carry the tree the admin form builds, as Magento stores it: every node has a type , a leaf has attribute , operator and value , a group has aggregator ( all / any ), value ( 1 = true) and conditions . Types may be short — Combine , Address , Product\Found , Product\Subselect , Product for cart rules, Combine and Product for catalog rules — or full class names; every type must be a Magento condition class, anything else is refused with the row number. Operators are Magento's: == , != , >= , <= , > , < , {} (contains), !{} , () (is one of), !() . A cart rule for orders of 100 or more or any product of category 12: {"type":"Combine","aggregator":"any","value":"1","conditions":[ {"type":"Address","attribute":"base_subtotal","operator":">=","value":"100"}, {"type":"Product\\Found","value":"1","aggregator":"all","conditions":[ {"type":"Product","attribute":"category_ids","operator":"()","value":"12"}]}]} The export writes exactly this form (with full class names), so the easiest way to a complex rule is: build one in the admin, export, copy. What a run does ¶ Every row is checked: name, websites and groups exist, dates, action, numbers, coupon type, the condition JSON (every type), categories exist. A dry run counts created and updated rules and names every problem with the row number; nothing is written. Catalog price rules need applying after the import, as after a change in the admin: Marketing › Catalog Price Rules › Apply Rules , or the catalogrule_rule indexer (cron does it when the indexer is scheduled). Auto-match knows Regel , Gutschein , coupon , Rabatt , discount , percent , Kundengruppen , from , to , SKUs , Mindestbestellwert , subtotal and the like. docs.text: Runs, dry runs and safety ¶ A run reads one file through a profile. Runs are queued (admin buttons, schedules, the CLI) and executed by OpenImport's own cron group or by bin/magento openimport:run ; never inside a web request. What happens in a run ¶ Read the file (see File formats ). Row filters skip rows (counted as filtered ). Mapping and transforms build Magento's import rows; a row that cannot be mapped becomes an error with its row number in your file. Behaviour : Only add new skips records that exist, Only update existing skips records that do not (counted as skipped ). Delta (when switched on): a record whose prepared rows are exactly what the last successful run of this profile sent is skipped (counted as unchanged ). Changing the profile's source, format, filters, behaviour, mapping or value maps forgets the stored state, and a run with full ignores it. Each line of the file is compared on its own, so a file with one line per store view (or several addresses or tier prices per record) only sends the lines that changed. Magento validates and imports the rows with its own import engine. Its errors are reported against the rows of your file, not against Magento's internal row numbers. Prepared rows are written to the run folder ( var/openimport/runs/<run id>/ ), so memory use does not grow with the file. Dry runs ¶ A dry run does everything except the import: Magento validates every row, and OpenImport compares the prepared rows with what the shop has now. The run page shows the totals (new, changed, unchanged, deleted) and a sample of up to 200 records per kind with before → after for every changed field. Comparison follows Magento's rules: empty cells change nothing, numbers compare as numbers (12.50 = 12.5), Yes/No equal 1/0. Products and customers are compared field by field; categories, images and product relations are not compared. Errors ¶ Stop on error (default): if any row has an error, nothing is imported. Skip rows with errors : valid rows are imported as long as the number of errors stays within allowed errors . Every error names the row in your file, the record's identifier, the field and what is wrong. The first 10,000 errors of a run are stored (setting Errors kept per run ); the count includes all of them. Safety threshold ¶ Runs with the Delete or Replace behaviour that would affect more than the safety threshold (default 10 % of the records of that kind in the shop) stop with the status Needs confirmation and do nothing. Confirming the run (typing DELETE or REPLACE in the admin, or --confirm on the CLI) runs it. Statuses ¶ Status Meaning Queued Waiting for the next cron minute (or the CLI). Running Being processed. Success Everything went through. Partial Valid rows were imported, some rows had errors. Failed Nothing was imported; the message says why. Needs confirmation Above the safety threshold; nothing was done. Cancelled Stopped by an admin before it started. Only one run of a profile runs at a time, and only one live import per kind of record (products, customers …), so two imports never fight over the same indexers.
