docs.text: Schedules and cron ¶ Magento Open Source has no scheduled import or export (that is Adobe Commerce only). OpenImport brings its own, run by Magento's normal cron. What you need ¶ Magento's cron must run every minute, as for any store: * * * * * php /var/www/html/bin/magento cron:run OpenImport adds its own cron group, openimport , which runs in a separate process. A long import never holds up Magento's default jobs (indexers, e-mails), and they never hold up an import. Job When What it does openimport_tick every minute Queues the runs of profiles whose schedule is due, then runs queued runs until the minute's time budget is used. openimport_cleanup hourly (minute 17) Removes old run folders, unused uploads and old schedule records; marks runs that stopped without finishing as failed. Without cron, queued runs wait. bin/magento openimport:queue:run does the same work as the tick by hand (see Command line ). Profile schedules ¶ A profile's schedule is a preset (every 15 or 30 minutes, every hour, every day at a time you choose, every night at 02:00, weekdays at 06:00) or a 5-field cron expression, and the form shows the next three run times: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Lists ( 1,15 ), ranges ( 8-18 ), steps ( */15 ) and names ( mon-fri , jan ) work. Times are read in the store's time zone (Stores › Configuration › General › Locale Options › Timezone), so 0 2 * * * means 02:00 local time, also across daylight-saving changes. A schedule only fires while the profile's Schedule is on switch is on. New and duplicated profiles start with it off: run a dry run first, then switch it on. A schedule needs a source that changes by itself: a profile that reads an uploaded file cannot be switched on (it would import the same file again and again; use a server folder, web address, SFTP or FTP), and a scheduled export needs a destination other than Download (a server folder, SFTP, FTP or e-mail). Scheduled runs are live runs. The safety threshold still applies: a scheduled Delete or Replace run that would remove more than the threshold stops with "needs confirmation" and waits for someone to confirm it on the run page. Exactly once ¶ Each due minute fires once, even when: two cron processes overlap (a slow cron:run and the next one): the first process records schedule:<profile>:<minute> in openimport_lock ; the second finds the record and does nothing; cron comes late: a due minute missed by up to 10 minutes still fires, once. Missed by more, it is skipped, and the next due minute fires as usual (no flood of catch-up runs after downtime); a run of the same profile is still going: the new run waits in the queue until the profile lock is free. Two runs of one profile never run at the same time, and two live imports of the same entity never run at the same time (products and Stock & prices share the product entity). Housekeeping ¶ Run files (the uploaded or fetched source, prepared rows, output) are removed after "Keep run files for" days (Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport). The run, its counts and stored errors stay. Uploaded files no profile uses any more are removed after two days. A run that has been "running" for more than 90 minutes without a live lock (the PHP process died, the server restarted) is marked failed with "The run stopped without finishing", so the profile can run again. docs.text: Magento's cron must run every minute, as for any store: * * * * * php /var/www/html/bin/magento cron:run OpenImport adds its own cron group, openimport , which runs in a separate process. A long import never holds up Magento's default jobs (indexers, e-mails), and they never hold up an import. Job When What it does openimport_tick every minute Queues the runs of profiles whose schedule is due, then runs queued runs until the minute's time budget is used. openimport_cleanup hourly (minute 17) Removes old run folders, unused uploads and old schedule records; marks runs that stopped without finishing as failed. Without cron, queued runs wait. bin/magento openimport:queue:run does the same work as the tick by hand (see Command line ).

docs.text: A profile's schedule is a preset (every 15 or 30 minutes, every hour, every day at a time you choose, every night at 02:00, weekdays at 06:00) or a 5-field cron expression, and the form shows the next three run times: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Lists ( 1,15 ), ranges ( 8-18 ), steps ( */15 ) and names ( mon-fri , jan ) work. Times are read in the store's time zone (Stores › Configuration › General › Locale Options › Timezone), so 0 2 * * * means 02:00 local time, also across daylight-saving changes. Scheduled runs are live runs. The safety threshold still applies: a scheduled Delete or Replace run that would remove more than the threshold stops with "needs confirmation" and waits for someone to confirm it on the run page.

docs.text: Each due minute fires once, even when: two cron processes overlap (a slow cron:run and the next one): the first process records schedule:<profile>:<minute> in openimport_lock ; the second finds the record and does nothing; cron comes late: a due minute missed by up to 10 minutes still fires, once. docs.text: Security ¶ OpenImport fetches files from other servers, reads formats that can carry attacks, and writes into the catalog. This page lists what the module does about that, what the settings control, and what remains your job. Admin actions ¶ Every controller is behind an ACL resource: View profiles , Create and edit profiles , Run profiles , Confirm runs above the safety limit , View runs and error reports , Manage connections , plus the configuration section. Roles that may view but not edit get a read-only form. Everything that changes state is a POST with Magento's form key; everything that reads is a GET. File answers go through Magento's FileFactory , never a raw path. Uploads: 256 MB at most, only .csv .tsv .txt .xlsx .json .xml , stored under a random token in var/openimport/tmp and removed by housekeeping. A token is accepted only if it names a file in that folder (no .. , no other folder). Sample and preview answers, error reports and the run page escape every value; messages from Magento's importer are shown as text. Remote sources and destinations ¶ Web address: http and https only, no credentials in the URL. The host is resolved and every address must be public: loopback, private (RFC 1918), link-local (169.254.x, the cloud metadata address), carrier-grade NAT, IPv6 ULA and link-local, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 are refused. The request is pinned to the checked address ( CURLOPT_RESOLVE ), every redirect hop is checked again, basic auth and bearer tokens are sent to the first host only, and downloads stop at 256 MB. Hosts you trust (a warehouse system on the LAN) go into Allowed private hosts . Server folder: only var/openimport and the folders listed in Allowed folders (absolute paths, real paths compared, so symlinks out of the sandbox do not help). Patterns pick files; the module never runs them. SFTP / FTP: host names are resolved and checked like URLs. SFTP uses phpseclib (password or private key, with an optional passphrase); FTP uses PHP's ftp_* functions with TLS when switched on, passive mode. Nothing is executed on the remote side; the module lists, downloads, uploads, renames and deletes inside the configured folder. E-mail destination: attachments are capped (setting), the recipients come from the profile, never from the file. Credentials ¶ Passwords, private keys, passphrases and tokens are encrypted with Magento's encryptor and stored under a separate secrets key of the profile. They are never written to logs, run messages, JSON profile exports, the admin form (the form shows "stored" and lets you replace a secret, not read it) or the error report. After a key rotation run bin/magento openimport:secrets:reencrypt . File formats ¶ XML: streamed with XMLReader ; documents with a DOCTYPE are refused, so there is no entity expansion and no external entity. The parser never resolves URLs. Archives (ZIP, gzip, tar): the file inside is written under a fixed name (entry names never become paths: no zip-slip), its size is counted while unpacking (1 GB limit, zip bombs), links are skipped, nested archives and password-protected entries are refused. See Archives . XSLT: stylesheets run with every read and write permission of libxslt switched off (no document() , no xsl:include / xsl:import , no files, no network), no PHP functions, no DOCTYPE in the stylesheet or the file, a size limit for the file (a DOM holds it whole). See XSLT . ODS: as XLSX (no DOCTYPE, no network, 512 MB unpacked limit), streamed with XMLReader. XLSX: read from the zip with size checks; a workbook whose parts would unpack to more than 512 MB is refused (zip bombs). Only the parts the reader needs are opened. CSV written by the module (error reports, exports): cells starting with = + - @ or a tab are prefixed with an apostrophe when the formula guard setting is on (default), so a product name cannot become a spreadsheet formula. Expressions and transforms: the expression language is parsed once per run into a small AST and evaluated without eval ; it has no access to PHP functions, files or the database. Division by zero and type errors become row errors. Writing into Magento ¶ Magento's own importer validates and writes every row. OpenImport does not write catalog tables itself. Runs that would delete or replace more records than the profile's safety threshold stop and wait for a typed confirmation by a user with the Confirm runs above the safety limit resource. New profiles always start with a dry run. One run per profile and one live import per core entity at a time (database locks with heartbeats), so two cron ticks cannot import the same file twice. What stays with you ¶ Protect var/openimport like the rest of var/ : it holds uploaded and fetched files and the error reports. Give SFTP/FTP accounts the smallest folder they need; the module cannot escape its folder, but the account could. Keep Magento's cron under a user that cannot write to the code base. Report problems privately, see SECURITY.md .

docs.text: Shipments and tracking numbers ¶ Since 1.5. Entity Shipments and tracking numbers ( openimport_shipment ), import only. A file from the warehouse or the carrier ships orders through Magento's own shipment service ( ShipOrderInterface ): stock, order state, shipment e-mails and the order history are exactly what the admin's Ship button does. Columns ¶ Column Required Meaning increment_id yes The order number as the customer sees it ( 100000123 ). item_sku no One item of the order. Empty: everything that is still open is shipped. A child's SKU (configurable, bundle) finds its parent. qty no How many of that item; needs item_sku . Empty: all that is left of the item. carrier_code no ups , dhl , fedex , usps , a carrier of an installed shipping module, or custom (the default when a tracking number has no carrier). title no The name shown with the tracking number; empty: the carrier's name. tracking_number no Empty: a shipment without a tracking number. notify no 1 , yes or true : send the shipment e-mail to the customer. comment no A comment on the shipment (not visible to the customer). Rows of the same order in one file make one shipment : all their items, all their tracking numbers. Two shipments of one order are two runs (or two files). What a run does ¶ Every row is checked first: the order exists and can be shipped, the item is open, the quantity is within what is left, the carrier is known. A dry run shows how many shipments would be made and names every problem with the file's row number. With When a row has an error → stop , nothing is shipped while one row is wrong. An order that already carries one of the file's tracking numbers, or has nothing left to ship, is skipped and reported (the run ends as partial ): the same file can be imported twice without a second shipment. Behaviour: Add/Update or Only add . There is nothing to update, replace or delete. Auto-match knows Bestellnummer , order number , Sendungsnummer , tracking , carrier , Menge and the like. Sample file: order;sku;qty;carrier;tracking;notify 100000123;;;dhl;00340434161094015902;1 100000124;SHIRT-RED-M;1;ups;1Z999AA10123456784;1 100000124;SHIRT-RED-L;1;ups;1Z999AA10123456784;

docs.text: Reviews, newsletter, search terms, synonyms, category positions ¶ Since 1.5. Five small entities, each import (Add/Update, Delete) and export, each a round trip: export a store, import the file into another, export again, same rows. Replace is refused for all of them. Product reviews ( openimport_review ) ¶ Reviews with ratings, matched by product SKU, nickname and title (or review_id , which the export writes). Column Required Meaning product_sku yes The reviewed product. nickname , title , detail new reviews Author name, summary, text. status no approved , pending or not approved ; new reviews: approved. store_codes no Store views the review is shown in, comma-separated, or all ; new reviews: all. created_at no The date ( 2025-02-03 10:00:00 ); empty: now. customer_email no Links the customer with that e-mail on the store view's website (the review stays a guest review when empty). ratings no Quality:4, Value:5 — the shop's ratings (Stores › Rating) by name with a value from 1 to 5. Replaces the review's votes. The product's review summary (stars on the product page) is recalculated after each review. Delete removes the reviews named by product, nickname and title. Newsletter subscribers ( openimport_newsletter ) ¶ Column Required Meaning email yes The subscriber, matched on the store view's website. store_code no The store view; empty: the default store view. status no subscribed (the default for new rows), unsubscribed , not activated , unconfirmed . A customer with that e-mail on the website is linked to the subscription. No e-mail is sent — no confirmation, no welcome, no unsubscribe notice — this is a data import, not a sign-up form. Delete removes the subscriptions. Search terms ( openimport_search_term ) ¶ Column Required Meaning query_text yes The term as typed, matched per store view. store_code no Empty: the default store view. redirect no A URL the search redirects to; an empty cell on an existing term removes the redirect. display_in_terms no 1 / 0 : shown among the popular search terms. popularity no The counter; num_results is exported but not imported (Magento fills it on the next search). Search synonyms ( openimport_search_synonym ) ¶ Column Required Meaning synonyms yes At least two words, comma-separated: shirt, tee, top . scope no all (every store view, the default), website:base , store:de ; a bare code is tried as a store view, then a website. A group is matched by its words and scope. A word that already sits in another group of the same scope merges the two groups, as the admin form does. Delete removes the group that holds the words. Product positions in categories ( openimport_category_position ) ¶ Column Required Meaning category_path yes The category by path ( Default Category/Men/Shirts ), as the category import. product_sku yes The product. position no The sort position in the category; empty keeps an existing position (new assignments: 0). Add/Update assigns the product to the category (when it is not in it yet) and sets the position; Delete removes the product from the category. The export writes every product-category assignment, so a file of one store's merchandising lands in another. What a run does ¶ Every row is checked first (the product, category, store view, customer, rating or scope exists; statuses, dates and numbers are valid; the same record is not in the file twice). A dry run counts and names every problem with the row number. Writes go through Magento's review, subscriber, search query, synonym group and category link models and repositories — the same code the admin forms use, so indexers, caches and summaries follow.

docs.text: Sources: where a profile reads its file ¶ Step 2 of the profile form. Every source delivers one file per run; the run keeps a copy in var/openimport/runs/<run id>/ (removed after "Keep run files for" days). Source Settings Notes Upload a file the file, uploaded in the form The same file is read again on every run until another one is uploaded; it cannot be scheduled. Server folder folder, file name pattern, which file, move-to folder A folder under var/openimport/ (for example supplier/incoming ), or an absolute path inside a folder allowed under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety › Extra server folders . Anything else is refused, also through symbolic links. Web address (URL) address, login (none, user name and password, bearer token), sheet gid http and https. A Google Sheets link (shared "anyone with the link" or published) is read as CSV; gid picks the sheet. SFTP server, port, user name, password or private key (+ passphrase), remote folder, pattern, which file, move-to Key login with an OpenSSH or PEM key, pasted into its multi-line field (a key that lost its line breaks is repaired before the login). FTP server, port, user name, password, explicit TLS (FTPS), passive mode, remote folder, pattern, which file, move-to Google Drive / Sheets (login) saved Google connection, folder link, id or path, pattern, which file, move-to Private files and Sheets (Sheets are read as Excel files); see Google Drive and Google Sheets . Dropbox , OneDrive / SharePoint saved connection, folder path, pattern, which file, move-to See Dropbox and OneDrive and SharePoint . REST API saved REST connection, path, records path, pages JSON answers, paged; see REST APIs . Amazon S3 / S3-compatible saved S3 connection, folder in the bucket, pattern, which file, move-to Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, MinIO, Garage and other S3-compatible services; the login is always a saved connection . For SFTP and FTP, Saved connection picks a login saved under System › Data Transfer › OpenImport Connections instead of entering it in the profile (since 1.4); see Saved connections . Any source may deliver a ZIP, gzip or tar archive: the file inside is read, see Archives . XML files can go through an XSLT stylesheet before they are read. Test connection checks the settings as they are in the form (saved or not) and says what the next run would read, without importing anything. Which file ¶ For folders and servers, the pattern picks the candidates ( * any text, ? one character, case does not matter, several patterns separated by commas: stock-*.csv, Stock-*.xlsx ), and Which file picks one of them: the newest (by modification time, the usual choice for a drop folder), the oldest (process a backlog in order, one file per run), or the first or last by name ( 2026-10-14.csv style names). A run with no matching file fails with a plain message and nothing else happens. All matching files, one run each (since 1.3) reads every matching file: the run takes the first file by name ( stock-2.csv before stock-10.csv ) and queues one run per other file, so every file has its own report, error list and move after success. The run message says File 1 of 3: stock-1.csv. The other files are queued as runs 12, 13. Files that another queued run of the profile already has are left to it, so a schedule never imports a file twice. When a file fails : Go on with the next file (default; the failed file stays for the next run) or Stop : the queued runs of the batch are cancelled and their files wait for the next run. After a successful run ¶ Source file after a successful run (step 6) applies to folders and servers: Keep it : the file stays; the next run reads it again unless a newer one arrives (delta mode makes that cheap). Move it to the processed folder : moved into the Move processed files to subfolder (default processed ), with the date and time added to the name when a file with that name is already there. Delete it . Only live runs that imported something (success or partial) move or delete; dry runs and runs started with a file of their own (CLI --file ) never touch the source. If the move or deletion fails after the import, the run stays successful and its message says what did not work. Secrets ¶ Passwords, private keys, passphrases and tokens are encrypted with Magento's key ( app/etc/env.php ) and stored in the profile. They are never sent back to the form (it only says that a value is stored; leave the field empty to keep it, type a new one to replace it), never exported with a profile and never logged. Saved connections keep theirs the same way. After bin/magento encryption:key:change , run bin/magento openimport:secrets:reencrypt . Safety ¶ URL sources only reach public addresses. Private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses ( 10.x , 192.168.x , 127.x , 169.254.x , fd00::/8 , …) are refused, also when a public host name resolves to one or a redirect leads there. Every redirect hop is checked again, and the request goes to the address that was checked. An administrator can allow a host name under Stores › Configuration › iranimij › OpenImport › Safety › Private hosts allowed as URL sources , for a feed from an internal system. docs.text: Quantities as changes ¶ Since 1.3. Some systems send what changed, not what is in stock: a delivery of 5, three sold in the shop on the corner. Step 5, Quantities in the file : are the new stock (default): the quantity replaces the current one, as in Magento's import; are changes (+5, -3) : the quantity is added to the current one. +5 adds five, -3 takes three away, a plain 4 adds four. Decimals take a comma or a point ( +2,5 ). It works for Products , Stock & prices (column qty , Magento's default stock) and Stock per source (MSI) (column quantity , per SKU and source). The current quantity is read for each batch, and a SKU that appears twice in a file adds up ( +5 then +2 on 10 gives 17). Magento receives one row per SKU (per SKU and source) with the result, after the file's last row. A product that does not exist yet starts at 0. A value that is not a change ( many ) is a row error naming the column. Live runs hold the lock of Magento's entity: products, Stock & prices and Stock per source runs never change the same quantities at the same time. The dry run shows the quantity Magento would receive ( qty: 10 → 17 ). Skip unchanged rows cannot be used together with it: the same +5 in tomorrow's file is a new delivery.

Transforms and expressions ¶ Every mapped field can run a list of transforms, in order, on the value taken from the source column (or the static value). Each step gets the previous step's result. Empty values stay empty in number and date transforms, so an empty price never turns into 0. A value a transform cannot handle (text in a number transform, an impossible date) becomes a row error naming the field, the step and the value; the rest of the file still imports. Text ¶ Transform Arguments Example trim – " Shirt " → Shirt lower , upper , title – red shirt → Red Shirt (title) replace find, replace (default: nothing) replace("cm", " cm") : 10cm → 10 cm regex pattern, replace (default: nothing) regex("^ART-(\d+)$", "$1") : ART-0042 → 0042 strip_html –

Soft & warm

→ Soft & warm prefix , suffix text prefix("DE-") : 42 → DE-42 (empty values stay empty) default value used when the value is empty fill_down group column (optional) an empty value takes the last value above it, within rows with the same group value (since 1.3; Shopify writes a title only on a product's first row) split separator, position (1 = first, -1 = last) split(";", 2) : a;b;c → b join separator, column, … join(" ", "Brand") : Shirt → Shirt ACME ; empty parts are left out Regex patterns are written without delimiters and are Unicode-aware; (?i) at the start ignores case. A pattern that backtracks too much fails the row instead of hanging the run. Numbers ¶ Numbers are read the way files write them: 1234.5 , 1,5 , 1.234,56 , 1,234.56 , 1 234,5 , 1'234.50 . Transform Arguments Example decimal_comma – for files with decimal commas: 1.234,50 → 1234.5 , 1.234 → 1234 number decimals (optional), decimal separator . or , (optional) number(2) : 5 → 5.00 ; number(2, ",") : 12.5 → 12,50 (exports) math operator ( + - * / , × ÷ , or add , subtract , multiply , divide ), operand math("*", 1.19) round decimals (default 2), mode half_up / up / down / ending , ending round(2, "ending", .99) : 12.30 → 12.99 price_adjust percent, decimals (default 2) price_adjust(10) : 19.99 → 21.99 round with mode ending moves to the next price with the given cents: 12.30 → 12.99 , 12.99 stays, and with .49 : 12.60 → 13.49 . Expressions ¶ expr(expression) computes a value from the whole source row. Expressions are parsed once per run; there is no eval and no access to PHP functions. Element Syntax Column {Column Name} (a } inside a name is written }} ) Current value value Text 'text' or "text" (a doubled quote inside is one quote) Number 42 , 1.5 , 1e3 (start with a digit: 0.5 , not .5 ) Arithmetic + - * / % Join text . ( {Brand} . ' ' . {Name} ) Compare = != <> < <= > >= (numbers as numbers, text ignoring case) Logic and , or , not , true , false Functions: IF(condition, then, else) , ROUND(number, decimals) , CONCAT(…) , LOWER(text) , UPPER(text) , TRIM(text) , COALESCE(…) (first non-empty), LEN(text) , NUMBER(text) , REPLACE(text, find, replace) , CONTAINS(text, part) , MIN(…) , MAX(…) , ABS(number) . Function names and keywords ignore case. Rules: Arithmetic with an empty value gives an empty value: {Special price} * 1.19 stays empty when there is no special price. Text that is not a number in arithmetic, and division by zero, are row errors. Empty text, 0 and false are false in conditions; everything else is true. Whole numbers keep every digit; decimals have 15 significant digits. Expressions are limited to 2,000 characters and 40 levels of nesting. Examples: IF({Stock} > 0, 1, 0) ROUND(NUMBER({Preis}) * 1.19, 2) CONCAT({Brand}, ' ', {Model}, ' ', {Color}) IF(CONTAINS({Category}, 'sale'), {Price} * 0.9, {Price}) COALESCE({EAN}, {GTIN}, {Supplier SKU}) Your own transforms ¶ Implement Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Transform\TransformProviderInterface and add the class to the providers argument of Iranimij\OpenImport\Model\Transform\TransformPool in your module's di.xml . A provider may also replace a built-in transform by using its name. Only when ¶ Since 1.3. Every transform can have a condition: type it into Only when before you add the transform. The transform then runs only for rows where the condition is true; other rows keep the value as it is. Conditions are expressions (see above) and can use the row's columns and value , the value at that step. Transform Only when Effect Change price by % (15) {Brand} = 'Acme' Acme prices +15 %, other brands unchanged Change price by % (-10) CONTAINS({Category}, 'sale') 10 % off in the sale category Round (0, ending, .99) value > 20 only prices above 20 end in .99 In the profile JSON a conditional transform is written as {"name": "price_adjust", "args": ["15"], "when": "{Brand} = 'Acme'"} .

docs.text: URL keys and redirects ¶ Since 1.3. Two settings in step 5 of a product profile. URL keys from a pattern ¶ Magento makes a product's URL key from its name. Supplier files often have many products with the same name, and Magento then refuses the second one. URL keys from a pattern builds the key from any mapped fields: Pattern Name, SKU URL key {name}-{sku} Blaue Jacke, J-100 blaue-jacke-j-100 {manufacturer}-{name} Acme, Hammer acme-hammer Fields are Magento fields in braces; they must be mapped in step 4. Text is transliterated ( ü → u ), lower case, words joined by hyphens, as Magento does it. Only rows whose URL key cell is empty get one, so a mapped url_key column always wins. A store view gets its own key when it has its own values for the pattern (a German name), otherwise it inherits. A key that another product has already, or that the pattern makes twice in one file, is a row error naming the other SKU: The URL key "hammer" belongs to H-2 already. Redirect old URLs (301) ¶ When a product's URL key changes, its old address answers with a permanent redirect to the new one, so links, bookmarks and search results keep working. OpenImport asks Magento's import to keep the URL history (the import column save_rewrites_history ), the same as the admin's Create Permanent Redirect for old URL .

docs.text: URL rewrites ¶ Since 1.5. Entity URL rewrites ( openimport_url_rewrite ), import and export. A file of old addresses and where they should go — after a relaunch, a shop migration, a campaign — lands in Magento's URL rewrites ( Marketing › URL Rewrites ): permanent (301) and temporary (302) redirects, or plain rewrites that show another page under the address. The export writes every rewrite of the shop, Magento's generated ones included, and imports back as it is. Columns ¶ Column Required Meaning request_path yes The address as the visitor types it, after the store's base URL: old-shirts.html , sale/summer . No spaces, # or // . store_code no The store view ( default , de ); empty: the default store view. A rewrite exists once per request path and store view. target_path custom Where it goes: a path of the shop ( new-shirts.html , catalog/category/view/id/5 ) or, for a redirect, a full address ( https://example.com/promo ). Empty when the row names a product, category or CMS page. redirect_type no 301 (permanent), 302 (temporary), or empty/ 0 for a plain rewrite that shows the target under the request path. Words work too: permanent, temporary. product_sku no The product the address belongs to. With a redirect, the target is the product's current URL in that store view ( blue-shirt.html ); without, its canonical path. category_path no The category by path ( Default Category/Men/Shirts ), same as the category import. cms_page no The CMS page by identifier ( about-us ). entity_type no custom , product , category or cms-page ; normally left empty, the filled column decides. The export writes it. description no A note shown in the admin grid. autogenerated , metadata no What the export writes for Magento's generated URLs ( 1 , and the category of a product-in-category URL as JSON). Leave empty in your own files. One of product_sku , category_path and cms_page at most; none of them makes a custom rewrite, which needs a target_path . What a run does ¶ Every row is checked: the path, the store view, the redirect type, the product/category/page exists, the target is not the request path itself, the same address is not in the file twice. A dry run counts what would be created and updated and names every problem with the row number. Add/Update creates a rewrite or updates the one that answers the request path in that store view (target, redirect type, entity, description). Delete removes the rewrites of the file. Replace is refused at save. Magento's generated URLs are never changed or deleted. A request path that is the URL Magento generated for another product, category or page is a conflict, reported with the owner: "blue-shirt.html" is the URL Magento generated for product SHIRT-BLUE; it cannot be changed. Magento regenerates those URLs on every save, so a change here would not last; change the product's URL key instead (the product import does that, with a 301 for the old address, see URL keys and redirects ). Auto-match knows old URL , new URL , from , to , redirect , SKU , alte URL , neue URL , Weiterleitung and the like. Sample file: request_path;target_path;redirect_type;product_sku;description old-shop/blue-shirt-xl.html;;301;SHIRT-BLUE-XL;Address from the old shop summer;sale/summer.html;302;;Campaign, remove in September shirts;catalog/category/view/id/12;;;Short address for the shirts category Export ¶ The export writes every rewrite with the store view code and, for product, category and CMS page rewrites, the SKU, category path or page identifier instead of Magento's internal ids, so the file is readable and imports into another store whose ids differ. Filter it in step 3 (for example autogenerated equals 0 for your own rewrites only, or request_path starts with a prefix).
